report_name: Massive Data Leak Exposes Two Billion Credentials from Infostealer Ops

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: Infostealer malware harvested credentials, including saved browser credentials, from millions of infected devices. These credentials were then aggregated in the exposed database.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: Infostealer malware campaigns stole web session cookies from infected user devices, which were then aggregated in the exposed database.

attack_patterns.name: Credential Stuffing
attack_patterns.description: The two billion exposed credentials create a severe risk of attackers using the leaked username/password pairs in large-scale automated attempts to log into a wide variety of other online services.

malware.name: Infostealer Malware
malware.description: A general class of malware designed to covertly infect devices and steal sensitive information. The article mentions RedLine, Vidar, and Raccoon as examples. Data stolen by these campaigns was aggregated in the discovered database.

identities.name: Jeremiah Fowler
identities.description: Cybersecurity researcher who discovered the unsecured database containing two billion credentials.

identities.name: ExpressVPN
identities.description: Collaborated with Jeremiah Fowler in reporting the discovery of the massive credential leak.

infrastructure.name: Unsecured Credential Aggregation Database
infrastructure.description: A massive, non-password-protected database found on the public internet, containing approximately two billion credentials in plaintext, aggregated from numerous infostealer malware operations.

indicators.name: Potential Credential Stuffing Attempt via Logon Failure
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Credential Stuffing Attempt via Logon Failure
id: 2b1a9c8d-e3f4-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
status: experimental
description: Detects a failed user logon attempt, which can be an indicator of a credential stuffing or password spraying attack. High rates of this event, especially from a single source, should be investigated.
references:
  - https://cybermagazine.com/news/expressvpn-how-infostealer-data-exposes-two-billion-logins
author: cyber.netsecio.io
date: 2026-11-25
tags:

  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
    Status: '0xc000006d'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Windows logon failures (Event ID 4625) with a status code indicating a bad username or password. A high rate of these events can be indicative of credential stuffing attacks, as mentioned in the article's detection section.
